root_idea.summary: The root presents two lexical axes: cutting away or turning aside, and a distinct anatomical term for a gland at the root of the jaw. The sense of proud aversion develops from the idea of turning away.
root_idea.development: The range includes removing or wiping away, something not cut off or drained, and shifting from one place or course to another. From this turning-away imagery come abstention and proud aversion; the related expression انتكف الأثر means to find a trace.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is Form X and is presented under the normalized perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To disdain or scorn something; to shrink from it with proud aversion or shame.
senses.usage_conditions: It governs مِنْ for the thing disdained and may be followed by أن plus an imperfect verb for an action regarded with disdain, as in refusing to be a servant of God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove or turn something aside; specifically, to wipe tears from the cheek with a finger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun النَّكْف is used for the act of wiping tears or removing them from the cheek.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be uncut off, undrained, or inexhaustible, said of abundant rain or a sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive construction describing something that cannot be cut off or drained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moving away from one land to another, or shifting from one matter or course to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun for departure or change away from an initial place or course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find or come upon a trace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression انتكف الأثر, ‘he found the trace.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abstain from or refuse to do something out of disdain and pride.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I, used with مِنْ to introduce the thing or action avoided.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wait, linger, or delay at a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ and a place or location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collective term for نَكَفَةٌ, a gland at the root of the jaw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun; of camels, the corresponding glands may be described as appearing or protruding.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I abstention or refusal from disdain and pride is represented as a Classical meaning.
The Form V meaning of waiting or lingering at a place is represented.
The Form X meaning of disdain, scorn, and shame-aversion is represented in the Quranic sense.
Pointer-only cross-reference; it supplies no definition or independent lexical statement.

cautions: All three Quranic occurrences are active Form X verbs; differences such as “will disdain,” “disdains,” and “disdained” reflect grammatical context rather than separate lexical senses.
